# Health

Right now Jordan is holding up reasonably well under sustained work stress, and the last month shows something like a turning point: the old pattern is still recognized in real time but isn't automatically winning anymore. Running has become the steadiest tool, and the shutdown-and-disappear spiral, while still present, is starting to get interrupted by actually telling people what's going on instead of going dark.

The through-line since late July has been the team restructuring at work. It started small on 7/30 with Marcus's vague "realignment" comments, and Jordan's response was already a tell — staying late for no real reason, then coming home to cereal for dinner and low energy. That withdrawal pattern repeated hard on 8/3 after Marcus tore apart the dashboard review: no dinner, phone off, two hours sitting in the dark while Pepper curled against him. Jordan named the pattern clearly that night — work criticism triggers a retreat inward, canceling plans, not reaching out, almost wanting to sit in the bad feeling before trying to climb out of it. It repeated again on 8/11 (canceling on Mika, not eating, sitting on the floor in the dark) after another whiplash round of feedback from Marcus. On 8/14, the stress surfaced as a genuinely disturbing recurring dream — an empty, flickering office, no one answering, no way out — which pulled Jordan out of sleep at 4am. That same day, Lena announced she's leaving the team, removing Jordan's main workplace ally and intensifying the sense of instability.

Against that, running at Greenwood Park became the consistent counterweight. The 7/31 run with Mika was the first real relief valve, and Mika's observation that day — that Jordan retreats from Coda whenever work gets shaky, and that Coda might be the real portfolio move — planted something that recurred later. Solo runs on 8/14 and 8/19 kept functioning as regulation: clearing the dream's residue, working through the lease decision, generally described as helping when little else did. The 8/19 run also marked a decision to renew the lease rather than move, settled mid-run on the hill trail.

The interview track with Northlight (phone screen 9/11, run afterward to burn off adrenaline) reframed the work stress somewhat — Jordan noted explicitly that the reorg situation hadn't changed, but having "a door" changed how heavy it felt. The third occurrence of the office dream on 9/14 was different from the first two: this time Jordan found the stairs and got out, which Jordan flagged as possibly meaningless but noticeable given the pattern. Also on 9/14, Jordan articulated the clearest health-relevant insight yet: the shutdown/disappear instinct is still there and still true in the moment, but it's stopped being the last word, because Jordan has been handing the hard stuff to Dev, Mom, and Lena instead of sitting with it alone.

Open threads: the actual reorg outcome is still pending, with Priya taking over as manager on 9/21 and the Northlight onsite on 9/24 — three days of a new manager before a personal day to interview elsewhere. Whether the withdrawal pattern holds up under a bad onsite outcome, or under Priya, is untested. No mention yet of sleep quality outside the dream disruptions, no medication or doctor visits noted in this period, and diet still seems to be a reliable barometer (skipped meals tracking closely with bad days) rather than something being managed on its own.
